description: Refactor the frontend state architecture so route pages own their own data, shareable page state lives in URL query parameters, and App.tsx becomes a small shell with global providers only. The goal is better maintainability, fewer broad rerenders, cleaner feature boundaries, and easier future work on SOP lookup, document review, extraction, and grounded chat.

userStories.title: Create route state refactor foundation
userStories.description: As a frontend maintainer, I want a small shared foundation for route-owned state so that pages can move out of the current large App-level state without duplicating feedback and invalidation plumbing.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a reusable feedback provider or equivalent hook for app-level success/error notices
Add shared query key helpers or a documented query key convention for feature hooks
Keep existing routes and navigation working with no behavior removal
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Move dashboard state into the dashboard route
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the dashboard page to fetch and own its own data so that unrelated pages do not rerender from dashboard state changes.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard route imports and calls only the data hooks it needs
Remove dashboard-specific props from the app-wide context/provider
Dashboard still shows source queue, archived counts, governance summary, and extraction status
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Move lookup state into URL-backed route state
userStories.description: As a CS user, I want lookup query, filters, selected quick answer, and selected SOP context to survive refresh and sharing so that lookup is predictable and easy to debug.
acceptanceCriteria: Lookup route owns lookup search state instead of receiving it from App.tsx
Persist lookup query and primary filters in URL query parameters using nuqs or the selected URL state helper
Opening a quick answer updates the right panel without a full page reload
Reloading the page preserves the lookup query and selected result when identifiers are available
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Move document review state into URL-backed route state
userStories.description: As a CS Ops reviewer, I want selected document, version, review filter, source status, and active unit state to live with the document review route so that the review workspace is deep-linkable and isolated.
acceptanceCriteria: Documents route owns selected document, selected version, selected unit, and review filter state
Persist selected document id, version id, unit id, and review filter in URL query parameters when possible
Approve/review unit actions use optimistic TanStack Query updates without causing page reload
Archive status is reflected in source queue and document detail after mutation without broad app refetches
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Move retrieval lab state into the retrieval route
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want retrieval testing state scoped to the retrieval page so that expensive search/test state does not live in the global app shell.
acceptanceCriteria: Retrieval lab route owns query, mode, filters, and result selection state
Persist retrieval query and search mode in URL query parameters
Retrieval mutations and result fetches invalidate only retrieval-related query keys
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Move synonyms state into the synonyms route
userStories.description: As a CS Ops user, I want synonym management filters and draft form state isolated to the synonyms page so that taxonomy work does not affect lookup or document review performance.
acceptanceCriteria: Synonyms route owns status filter, selected group, form draft, and sync action state
Persist synonym status filter and selected group id in URL query parameters when possible
Create, approve, reject, and sync actions invalidate only synonym-related query keys
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Move grounded chat state into the chat route
userStories.description: As a CS user, I want grounded chat state scoped to the chat page while still allowing a question to be seeded from the URL so that chat remains isolated from SOP lookup and document review.
acceptanceCriteria: Chat route owns thread messages, pending question, selected citation, and submit state
Support an optional URL query parameter for initial chat question
Chat answers render citations with actions to open quick answer or full SOP
Chat page does not answer without backend-provided citations
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Split frontend API hooks by feature
userStories.description: As a frontend maintainer, I want API hooks split by domain so that each page imports only the hooks it needs and large shared hook files stop becoming implicit global dependencies.
acceptanceCriteria: Split the current broad API hook file into feature-oriented hook modules for documents, lookup/search, synonyms, chat, dashboard, and shared utilities
Keep a compatibility barrel export only if it does not reintroduce circular dependencies
Each route imports feature hooks directly from the relevant module
No import cycles are introduced
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Simplify App shell and app context
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want App.tsx and app context to contain only shell-level concerns so that future feature work does not keep growing a god component.
acceptanceCriteria: App.tsx contains routing shell, providers, navigation state, and command/global search concerns only
Remove page-specific props from the app context after all migrated routes own their state
Route components no longer depend on one mega app context for feature data
Existing navigation, command access, and route rendering continue to work
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Add performance guardrails after state migration
userStories.description: As a product user, I want heavy pages to stay responsive so that document review, lookup, and chat remain usable with large SOP documents and many retrieval units.
acceptanceCriteria: Use deferred input state for global command/search inputs that trigger expensive filtering
Lazy-render or memoize heavy document review panels where it reduces unnecessary rendering without hiding current content
Scope TanStack Query invalidations to the smallest affected query key after mutations
Large text inputs for raw text upload avoid blocking keystrokes with expensive synchronous parsing
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
Typecheck passes
